title: Conditional contraction coefficients and their applications to quantum networks
authors: Christoph Hirche, Ian George, Theshani Nuradha, Mark M. Wilde
abstract: Contraction coefficients quantify the loss of distinguishability induced by a channel and provide a strong form of the data-processing inequality. While standard contraction coefficients ignore auxiliary quantum systems, existing extensions based on complete contraction coefficients require the compared states to have identical reference marginals. In this work, we introduce conditional contraction coefficients, a novel family that incorporates arbitrary quantum reference systems by subtracting the distinguishability already present in the reference system. We develop a general framework for contraction coefficients with such quantum side information, including the corresponding strong-data-processing-inequality (SDPI) constants, expansion coefficients, and relative contraction coefficients. For the trace distance, we show that the optimization can be restricted to orthogonal input states. For the quantum relative entropy, we prove that its conditional contraction coefficient is exactly equal to the contraction coefficient of the conditional mutual information, extending the classical correspondence between relative-entropy contraction and mutual-information contraction to the setting with quantum side information. More generally, we identify structural properties of divergences required for these results and discuss extensions beyond the relative entropy. These results establish a unified framework for analyzing information contraction in quantum network settings, where quantum side information and distributed correlations are intrinsic features of the information-processing task. Applications include an extension of the Polyanskiy-Wu bounds on mutual information contraction, new perspectives on mixing times, and fundamental limits on quantum memories.
summary: This work introduces conditional contraction coefficients to provide a robust measure of information loss in quantum channels when quantum side information is present. It unifies the analysis of information contraction by extending data-processing inequalities to include reference systems. The results establish fundamental limits for quantum networks and memory capacity by providing a comprehensive theoretical framework.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of quantifying information loss (distinguishability loss) through quantum channels when arbitrary quantum side information (reference systems) is present.
main_result: It introduces conditional contraction coefficients, establishing a unified framework for analyzing information contraction in quantum networks, and proving key equalities for the quantum relative entropy.
method: The authors develop a general mathematical framework by defining novel contraction coefficients based on the difference of divergences involving the reference system, extending existing data-processing inequalities.
model_or_system: The analysis centers on general quantum channels ($\mathcal{N}$) acting on quantum states, explicitly incorporating an arbitrary quantum reference system ($R$) to model side information.
key_observables: Conditional contraction coefficients ($\eta_{\Delta}^D(\mathcal{N})$), standard contraction coefficients ($\eta_D(\mathcal{N})$), and the conditional mutual information.
important_parameters: The type of quantum divergence used (e.g., trace distance, quantum relative entropy) and the presence/nature of the reference system $R$.
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the ability to define and manipulate divergences that account for side information, with specific results depending on properties like the extended direct-sum property.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes relationships between various contraction coefficients for the relative entropy, showing inequalities and equalities.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the novel conditional contraction coefficients, proving key identities (especially for relative entropy), establishing general inequalities between different types of coefficients, and concluding with applications to network bounds and memory limits.
why_interesting: The development of generalized information measures that explicitly account for side information is crucial for accurately modeling realistic quantum communication protocols and network constraints.

Figure 2: Status of tensorization of the relative-entropy SDPI constants considered in this work. Stabilization cannot decrease the corresponding coefficient. Green entries tensorize exactly for fixed product states and red entries do not tensorize in general. The ordinary SDPI nevertheless tensorizes under the sufficient conditions established in Corollary 9. Section C features a proof that the stabilized complete SDPI does not tensorize in general. For all quantities on the left side, we have an approximate tensorization result.
